candidate_sentences.text: During the 2025 financial year, AS Pro Kapital Grupp reported total revenue of EUR 53.2 million, marking a substantial increase compared to EUR 18.2 million in 2024.
Gross profit for the twelve months of 2025 rose to EUR 18.8 million compared to EUR 5.4 million in 2024, while fourth quarter gross profit reached EUR 6.9 million up from EUR 2.6 million.

Operating profit for 2025 improved dramatically to EUR 14.7 million from EUR 0.1 million in 2024, and the fourth quarter operating result increased to EUR 7.1 million compared to EUR 1.9 million in the corresponding period of the previous year.
Net profit for the twelve months of 2025 turned positive at EUR 12.0 million, representing a sharp improvement from the net loss of EUR 3.9 million reported in 2024.
Basic and diluted earnings per share for 2025 were EUR 0.22, compared to EUR -0.06 in 2024, while fourth quarter earnings per share rose to EUR 0.11 from EUR 0.01.
Operating cash flows improved to a positive EUR 10.8 million for 2025, recovering from cash used of EUR 10.4 million in 2024.
Total assets stood at EUR 124.5 million at the end of December 2025 compared to EUR 118.8 million a year earlier, while total liabilities decreased to EUR 61.2 million from EUR 67.5 million.
Total equity increased to EUR 63.3 million from EUR 51.2 million, and net asset value per share grew to EUR 1.12 from EUR 0.89 as of 31 December 2024.

verified_key_information_units.information: Revenue growth was primarily driven by the handover of completed residential units in the Kalaranna District and Uus-Kindrali developments in Tallinn, as well as the City Villas project in Vilnius, contrasting lower 2024 revenue due to delayed starts in Kalaranna and limited sales elsewhere.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report - Revenue from real estate sales section

candidate_sentences.text: The strong revenue growth was driven by the handover of completed apartments in the Kalaranna and Uus-Kindrali developments in Tallinn, as well as the City Villas project in Vilnius, following the signing of notarial sales agreements and the transfer of legal titles.

Conversely, revenue in the prior year remained lower because apartment handovers in the Kalaranna District only commenced in December 2024, with earlier sales restricted to remaining inventory in Latvia and Lithuania.

verified_key_information_units.information: Segmental revenue shifted significantly, with Estonia contributing 75% of total revenue in 2025 (versus 27% in 2024), Latvia's contribution falling to 0.3% (from 25%), and Lithuania maintaining a stable 12% share (versus 11% in 2024).
Liquidity and capital position improved, supported by active management of bank loans and bonds.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key performance indicators table; Financing sources and policies section

candidate_sentences.text: Total assets stood at EUR 124.5 million at the end of December 2025 compared to EUR 118.8 million a year earlier, while total liabilities decreased to EUR 61.2 million from EUR 67.5 million.

Financing activities during the year included the partial redemption of secured non-convertible bonds in the amount of EUR 9.405 million in August 2025, which reduced the total outstanding nominal amount of the bonds from EUR 19.95 million to EUR 10.545 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Major real estate developments advanced: completion of the white building in Uus-Kindrali (Tallinn) with 39 units closed by year-end (78% of sellable area sold); construction commenced on the Blue Marine project in Riga's Klīversala Quarter; first real rights agreements signed and units handed over in Šaltinių Namai Attico (Vilnius); and building permit obtained for the Borgo luxury residential complex in Vilnius (construction planned for H2 2026).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Chairman’s summary; Overview of the development projects section
